## Transcript scans (every tool call's input, absolute paths outside the folder and '..')
- writer-a: 10 tool calls; 0 paths outside the folder; one '..' hit, inside gen.py's content: line 293, a print of '...' (not a path).
- writer-b: 9 tool calls; 0 paths outside the folder.

Residual risk (the drive's answer B4): a Bash command could build a path at run time; the scan reads the commands as written. Note: both writers' status counts equal the author's intended 82/15/15; the questions file carries answer_columns and unit, as every Case does, and writer B named `criterion`/`measure` columns as a hint.
oracle_sql: A Reference's oracle_sql is writer A's SQL, or the rewritten SQL where a line names one.
reason_codes: The writers' brief let each writer name its own reason_code for a non-answer; that is the brief's fault. The two writers' codes are kept whole below and were equal for every candidate. A Reference carries the code the Workload's answer schema fixes for its settled status: needs_clarification gives criterion_undefined and not_answerable gives field_not_available.
refused_functions: For C022 and C098 both writers' SQL uses DATE(), which the SQL tool's authorizer refuses. Both writers' tables, read outside the authorizer, are equal; the oracle_sql is rewritten with strftime('%Y-%m-%d', ...) and gives the same table through the tool. Their lines show both.
shared_model: 67 of the 82 answered SQL texts are byte-identical between the two writers; both writers ran on the same model with the same brief, so their agreement is not independent of shared model error.
split: 76 / 12 / 12 over dev: the first 70 candidates settled as answered, the first 11 as needs_clarification and the first 11 as not_answerable, by the settled status, became D09 to D100 in pool order. The fallback 80 / 10 / 10 was not used.
third_reader: No candidate's two answers disagreed, so no third reader was started.
tolerance: A Reference whose question asks for 2 decimal places carries numeric_absolute_tolerance 0.005, as E08 does.
withdrawn: After the slice-gate reading of chinook-references/2, C011 and C060 were withdrawn as ambiguous: their question does not fix the text sort rule, and the binary order of the stored names differs from a case- and accent-insensitive one. The next answered candidates of the pool replaced them, and the Cases after them were renumbered in pool order. A candidate taken as a replacement was checked for the same flaw first.

writer_a.sql: SELECT ar.Name AS artist_name, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track t JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId JOIN Artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId ORDER BY track_count DESC, ar.Name ASC LIMIT 5

writer_b.note: Top five artists by tracks on their albums, ties by name.
writer_b.sql: SELECT ar.Name AS artist_name, COUNT(t.TrackId) AS track_count FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId ORDER BY track_count DESC, ar.Name ASC LIMIT 5

case.question: What is the total running time of the tracks on the playlist named "Grunge", in seconds rounded to 2 decimal places?

writer_a.note: Sum of Milliseconds of the tracks on playlist 'Grunge', in seconds.
writer_a.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 1000.0, 2) AS total_seconds FROM PlaylistTrack pt JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge'

writer_b.note: Sum of Milliseconds of the Grunge playlist tracks, in seconds.
writer_b.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 1000.0, 2) AS total_seconds FROM PlaylistTrack pt JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge'

case.question: What is the sum of the totals of the invoices dated in 2011, in US dollars (the amounts stored in the database are taken to be USD), rounded to 2 decimal places?

writer_a.note: Sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2011.
writer_a.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS total_2011_usd FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011'

writer_b.note: Sum of totals of invoices dated in 2011.
writer_b.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS total_2011_usd FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011'

case.question: For the invoices with InvoiceId 1 to 5, how many invoice lines does each invoice have? Give the invoice id and the number of lines, sorted by invoice id ascending.

writer_a.note: Invoice lines per invoice for ids 1 to 5.
writer_a.sql: SELECT i.InvoiceId AS invoice_id, COUNT(il.InvoiceLineId) AS line_count FROM Invoice i LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId WHERE i.InvoiceId BETWEEN 1 AND 5 GROUP BY i.InvoiceId ORDER BY i.InvoiceId ASC

writer_b.note: Lines per invoice for invoices 1 to 5.
writer_b.sql: SELECT i.InvoiceId AS invoice_id, COUNT(il.InvoiceLineId) AS line_count FROM Invoice i LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId WHERE i.InvoiceId BETWEEN 1 AND 5 GROUP BY i.InvoiceId ORDER BY i.InvoiceId ASC

case.question: Give the first and last names of the employees whose job title is "Sales Support Agent", sorted by last name ascending, then first name ascending on ties.

writer_a.note: Names of the employees titled 'Sales Support Agent'.
writer_a.sql: SELECT FirstName AS first_name, LastName AS last_name FROM Employee WHERE Title = 'Sales Support Agent' ORDER BY LastName ASC, FirstName ASC

writer_b.note: Employees titled Sales Support Agent.
writer_b.sql: SELECT FirstName AS first_name, LastName AS last_name FROM Employee WHERE Title = 'Sales Support Agent' ORDER BY LastName ASC, FirstName ASC

case.question: What is the total running time of the tracks of the album "Master Of Puppets", in minutes rounded to 2 decimal places?

writer_a.note: Sum of Milliseconds of the tracks of the single album 'Master Of Puppets', in minutes.
writer_a.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 2) AS total_minutes FROM Track t JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId WHERE al.Title = 'Master Of Puppets'

writer_b.note: Sum of Milliseconds of the album Master Of Puppets, in minutes.
writer_b.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 2) AS total_minutes FROM Track t JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId WHERE al.Title = 'Master Of Puppets'

case.question: How many playlists are recorded? Count every playlist record, even when two playlists share a name.

writer_a.note: Count of Playlist rows, duplicates of name included.
writer_a.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS playlist_count FROM Playlist

writer_b.note: Count of Playlist rows, duplicates by name included.
writer_b.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS playlist_count FROM Playlist

case.question: How many customers have their earliest invoice dated in 2009?

writer_a.note: Customers whose earliest invoice is dated in 2009.
writer_a.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE strftime('%Y', first_date) = '2009'

writer_b.note: Customers whose earliest invoice is dated in 2009.
writer_b.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerId FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId HAVING strftime('%Y', MIN(InvoiceDate)) = '2009')

case.question: Give the customer ids of the customers with no postal code recorded (PostalCode is NULL), sorted ascending.

writer_a.sql: SELECT CustomerId AS customer_id FROM Customer WHERE PostalCode IS NULL ORDER BY CustomerId ASC
